claim.statement: On the heroes-of-sokoban-ascii-v1 F.G instance, the supplied RR route reaches exact_win alive on the final key in three matching local model replays.

model.transition_semantics: UDLRA keys; alive; first win required on the final key
model.cost_semantics: number of UDLRA keys; no minimality claim

initial_state.goal: heroes occupy exactly the goal cells
initial_state.termination: alive and first win on final key

negative_controls.mutation: An invalid route promoted to VERIFIED

negative_controls.name: truncated_prefix_rejected
negative_controls.mutation: The final route key was dropped, leaving R
negative_controls.observed: python_spec_oracle and python_flat_bitmask_oracle both returned exact_win=false

negative_controls.name: post_win_extra_key_rejected
negative_controls.mutation: An extra U key was appended after the winning RR route
negative_controls.observed: python_spec_oracle and python_flat_bitmask_oracle both returned exact_win=false

limitations: VERIFIED is differential model_replay only; it is not model_proof and no formal proof or route minimality is claimed.
The three local engines can share a mistaken interpretation; external_spec_pinned=false and no live original-engine execution is claimed.
source_lock_asserted=false; checker pins preserve implementation/binary hashes but are not independent authenticity or correctness proofs.
The source trajectory commitment is its original 64-bit FNV-1a digest; the exported ASCII trajectory does not reconstruct hidden per-frame state for other boards.
Structural envelope validation alone does not independently accept the domain verdict; consumers must trust or independently rerun the pinned Soko verifier.

SimGrammar unbound: agent-pathfinding.yaml was inspected but not pinned because it owns agent route search and least-cost routing; this source only replays supplied RR keys and establishes neither route search nor minimality; mechanics=[].
